correctnessFindings.assessment: Crashpad already rejected dumps over 64 MiB at stat time. The capture now reads through the shared bounded reader before parsing, preventing a growing dump from bypassing that existing allowance.
Captured sizeBytes uses the actual buffer length rather than stale stat size. Read failure follows the existing null-result path, and the reservation is released in finally.

originalReview.userVisibleBeforeAfter: Normal accepted crash reports are unchanged. A dump that grows beyond the existing 64 MiB allowance during capture is skipped instead of being fully read and parsed.
originalReview.capacityAndDataLoss: Existing dump-source limit enforced during read. The source dump is not deleted or uploaded by this change, and no new privacy or process-liveness policy is introduced.

platformEvidence.assessment: The common file reader and minidump parsing path use portable Node APIs. Fresh macOS tests run controlled dump reads; a real native crash and file growth were not reproduced on Linux or Windows.
platformEvidence.executedHost: Fresh shared batch: macOS darwin arm64; Node 26.6.0. PRs outside that batch have no new execution in this follow-up.

originalReview.sshAndFolderCases: Crash reporting remains scoped to the existing runtime; this does not move remote files to the local host or infer remote process death. Workspace type is unrelated.
